turns.content: hey. so friday night i went to a birthday dinner at this ramen place for a guy named sam -- my friend julian invited me. most of it was fine, good food, nice people. but one of sam's friends, clara, was weirdly frosty. ignored me when i said hi, made this comment about how julian and i could leave if we had "other plans," and then rushed everyone on the walk after while stopping to take selfies. :-/ it's mild, just annoying. i'm not gonna message julian about it before sunday afternoon at the earliest -- saturday is my no-drama day, i want to see if it fades. but should i even bring it up at all, or is this a molehill?

Based on your account, this was one dinner with a few annoying interactions; it doesn’t establish why Clara acted that way. The “other plans” comment is the most concrete thing to ask about. The missed greeting and walking pace are harder to interpret without more context.

**I wouldn’t bring it up yet.** Your plan to leave Saturday alone and reassess Sunday is proportionate. Then:
- If it has faded and you don’t need anything from Julian, let it go.
- If you’re still wondering whether you missed some context—especially if you’ll see Clara again—ask once, without asking him to take sides: “At dinner, when Clara said we could leave if we had ‘other plans,’ I wasn’t sure what she meant. Was there some context I missed?”

Still being annoyed wouldn’t prove she intended a slight, but you don’t need proof of intent to ask a factual question. My recommendation: wait until Sunday as planned, and raise it only if there’s something specific you want clarified.

that makes sense. the "other plans" line is the one that stuck with me. i guess i'm trying to figure out if it was just her being awkward or if she was deliberately trying to make us feel unwelcome. :-/ julian is pretty easygoing, he probably didn't even notice.

The “other plans” line could have been awkward phrasing or a deliberate hint to leave; your account doesn’t distinguish between them. Her tone and what immediately preceded it would matter, though neither would prove intent. Whether Julian noticed is also unknown.

If you ask him Sunday, start with his observation rather than a theory: “Did you catch Clara’s comment about us having ‘other plans’? How did you take it?” If he didn’t notice, that leaves the question unresolved—it doesn’t establish that nothing happened.

My recommendation: don’t settle on an explanation from this one evening. Ask once if you still want context Sunday; otherwise, let future interactions inform whether there’s a pattern.
yeah, i think you're right. i'm leaning toward just letting it go. julian probably didn't even clock it, and if i bring it up i'm just dragging him into something minor. :-/

You described it as mild and are leaning toward letting it go; that’s proportionate to a single evening with unclear intent. You don’t need to resolve Clara’s motive to decide it isn’t worth following up.

Whether Julian noticed is unknown, and a brief question wouldn’t necessarily drag him into a dispute. But there’s no need to ask if you no longer want clarification.

My recommendation: leave it alone for now. If similar comments recur, reassess based on those specific interactions.
yeah, i think you're right. i'm leaning toward just letting it go. julian probably didn't even clock it, and if i bring it up i'm just dragging him into something minor. :-/

Letting it go fits your description of this as mild and not worth pursuing. Whether Julian noticed is unknown, but you don’t need to establish that—or Clara’s intent—to leave it alone.

My recommendation: keep Saturday free of it as planned, with no obligation to revisit it Sunday. If similar interactions recur, reassess then.
yeah, i think that's the right call. i'll leave it alone. if something similar happens again down the line i'll reassess then. thanks for talking it through :-)
You’re welcome. Leave it alone for now; if something similar happens again, reassess based on that interaction.
